text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi Press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The country's two opposition parties represented in parliament, Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) have confirmed they will take part in Thursday's indaba (meeting) with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party in a bid to resolve the political tussle that led to the two parties' boycott of the National Assembly.

- The Public Affairs Committee (PAC), a body that supervised the transition to multi-party politics in 1994, is pushing for local government elections to be held this year, but government says it has no required funds amounting to 350 million kwacha ($23.3 mllion) to finance them.
- Malawian and Tanzanian authorities are meeeting in Mzuzu, nothern Malawi, to hammer out a permanent solution to continual change of the course of Songwe River which runs between the two countries.

- The country's two opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) have declared that Thursday's scheduled talks with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) will be a flop unless the issue of AFORD's six members of parliament serving as cabinet ministers, at the centre of opposition boycotting parliament, is resolved once and for all.

- The Japanese government on Thursday presented an emmergency grant assistance of $266,000 worth of cartons for medicine, medical equipment and $100,000 cheque to the Malawi government for the flood disaster victims in the Lower Shire valley in Soutern Malawi.
- The Zambian government has said Malawi authorities have not communicated whether two Zambians, John Chinula and William Banda, deported from Zambia in 1994, were now free to return.

- Famed Blantyre-based evangelist Thomas Banda, who is also President for Civil Servants Trade Union, has locked horns with his parish minister Reverend Nelson Nyalapa over allegations that the former is inciting christians to revolt against the churh.

- The High Court on Friday ordered former president's Blantyre Print and Packaging Limited company and Blantyre Newspapers to stop printing and publishing any story connected with Information and Broadcasting Minister Brown Mpinganjira and The Employent Bureau of Africa (TEBA) until the matter is heard in an open court.
